source: src/database/engine/page_test.cc (netdata/netdata @ 1e97a0fc9e), hand-extracted; results of actually running it are in pgd-tests-run.json

facts.dispatch: `netdata -W pgd-tests` calls pgd_test(argc, argv) (src/daemon/main.c:432-433, inside #ifdef ENABLE_DBENGINE)
facts.have_gtest: HAVE_GTEST is defined nowhere: not in CMakeLists.txt, packaging/cmake, build/config.h, build/CMakeCache.txt, nor in the compile command of page_test.cc in build/compile_commands.json. The only references are page_test.cc:4,467,477. The production build therefore compiles the stub at page_test.cc:467-475, which prints 'Can not run PGD tests because the agent was not build with support for google tests.' and returns 0. Commit 2d974dc51d (#22955), which added the last three tests, says 'pgd-tests could not execute because that build lacks HAVE_GTEST'.
does_not_compile_with_gtest: PAGE_METRICS and PAGE_GORILLA_METRICS (page_test.cc:37,41,43,203,206,228,231,259,262,282,285) are defined nowhere; commit 00f897a883 (#17237, 2024-03-24) renamed them to RRDENG_PAGE_TYPE_ARRAY_32BIT (0) and RRDENG_PAGE_TYPE_GORILLA_32BIT (2) (rrddiskprotocol.h:43-46)
page_test.cc:462 calls pgc_destroy(dummy_cache); cache.h:178 declares pgc_destroy(PGC *cache, bool flush) since 932bbf3b4e (#19823)
facts.slots_do_not_fit: struct pgd has uint16_t used and uint16_t slots (page.c:32,35) and page_raw_t has uint16_t size (page.c:22), narrowed from uint32_t in 6b8c6baac2 (#18945, 2024-12-05). slots_for_page(1024 * 1024) returns 1048576 for gorilla (page_test.cc:43-44); pgd_create stores it as 0 (page.c:479), so the first pgd_append_point hits 'used >= slots' and calls pgd_fatal (page.c:951-953): 7 of the 11 tests die at their first append.
facts.internal_checks_off: NETDATA_INTERNAL_CHECKS is not defined in this build, so internal_fatal() is a no-op (libnetdata/log/nd_log-fatal.h:13-17); pgd_fatal/fatal are real and end in exit(1) (libnetdata/log/nd_log.c:509-596)
facts.page_type: page_type = PAGE_GORILLA_METRICS (page_test.cc:37); slots_for_page returns 1024 for PAGE_METRICS and n for PAGE_GORILLA_METRICS (page_test.cc:39-48); the switch statements in MemoryFootprint/DiskFootprint carry expectations for both
facts.storage_point_equality: operator== (page_test.cc:10-33) compares min, max, sum, start_time_s, end_time_s, count, flags; it does not compare anomaly_count. NaN points compare unequal.
